Call episomal ecDNA from AmpliconSuite output

Source: R/episomal_ampliconsuite.R
call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite.Rd

Classifies a single AmpliconClassifier ecDNA feature as episomal (simple-excision circle) or not, from its AmpliconArchitect graph and its ecDNA interval(s). The amplicon extent is taken from the AmpliconClassifier ecDNA interval BED (AA's own amplicon call) – no copy-number threshold is applied here. The feature is episomal when a BOUNDARY DUP exists: an intra-chromosomal DUP whose ends bracket the outer boundary of the ecDNA interval on its chromosome (lo <= interval start and hi >= interval end). The boundary DUP reported is the one with the highest read-pair support among spanning DUPs. A multi-chromosome ecDNA is chimeric episomal when every chromosome is bracketed by a boundary DUP and joined by >= 1 translocation.

Usage

call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(
  graph_file,
  intervals,
  tol = 0L,
  bridge_gap = 1e+06,
  min_occupancy = 0.05,
  trim_to_amplified = TRUE,
  min_seg_cn_frac = 0.1,
  structural_qc = TRUE,
  qc_amp_frac = 0.5,
  qc_src_frac = 0.5,
  qc_jcn_frac = 0.1,
  qc_edge_tol = 10000,
  ploidy = NULL,
  cnv_file = NULL,
  min_cn_ratio = 3,
  default_ploidy = 2
)

Arguments

graph_file

Path to the amplicon's AmpliconArchitect *_graph.txt.

intervals

The ecDNA feature's intervals: a path to an AmpliconClassifier *_ecDNA_<k>_intervals.bed, or a data.frame/data.table/GRanges-like object with chr/start/end. AmpliconClassifier's exclusive-end convention is handled internally.

tol

Integer; coordinate tolerance (bp) for the boundary-DUP bracket test (default 0; graph and interval coordinates come from the same graph so no tolerance is normally needed).

min_occupancy

Numeric in (0, 1]; minimum fraction of the boundary-DUP bracketed span that must be covered by the ecDNA intervals for an episomal call (default 0.05, i.e. reject when >95% of the bracketed span is non-amplified). A simple-excision circle is near-contiguous, so a DUP spanning a largely non-amplified region (e.g. a lone DUP across a diploid chromosome arm) is rejected as not a self-contained circle. The default was set by a PCAWG-vs-PURPLE concordance sweep (optimal at 2-5%; 5% additionally removes scattered low-occupancy secondary features).

trim_to_amplified

Logical; trim the AmpliconClassifier ecDNA interval to its amplified extent before the boundary-DUP test (default TRUE). AmpliconClassifier occasionally pads an interval with flanking diploid sequence, pushing the outer extent past the boundary DUP and mis-calling a clean episome as complex; trimming uses the AA graph's own segment copy numbers to drop leading/trailing near-diploid segments (edges only – internal low-CN segments are kept). It can only shrink the extent, so it may rescue a false-complex call but never breaks a true-episomal one.

min_seg_cn_frac

Numeric in (0, 1]; a segment counts as amplified for trim_to_amplified when its copy number is at least this fraction of the amplicon's peak segment copy number (default 0.10). Relative to the amplicon's own amplification, not a global ploidy cutoff.

structural_qc

Logical (default TRUE); apply structural quality control to a bracketed amplicon before calling it episomal, using the AA graph's own segment copy numbers, source (open-end) edges and junction copy numbers. Rejects (→ status = "complex") an amplicon that is not amplified at both boundary-DUP breakends, is OPEN at the boundary (a large source edge at a breakend), is closed by a boundary DUP whose copy number is far below the circle CN, or has an INV/TRA at a boundary out-copying the DUP. Ported from the PURPLE-native call_simple_excision(). Set FALSE for the older bracket-and-occupancy behaviour.

qc_amp_frac, qc_src_frac, qc_jcn_frac

Numeric in (0, 1]; the structural-QC thresholds, each relative to the width-weighted median copy number across the boundary-DUP span (the "circle-body" CN). A boundary breakend must be amplified to >= qc_amp_frac × circle CN (default 0.5); a boundary source edge >= qc_src_frac × circle CN marks an open boundary (default 0.5); the boundary DUP's junction copy number must be >= qc_jcn_frac × circle CN (default 0.1; a low floor that rejects only a boundary DUP explaining a tiny fraction of the amplification, while tolerating internally re-amplified episomes whose resident locus is boosted above the circularising junction's copy number — e.g. DO11854 EGFR).

qc_edge_tol

Integer; window (bp) around a boundary-DUP breakend within which a source edge or INV/TRA breakend counts as "at the boundary" (default 1e4).

ploidy, cnv_file

Tumour ploidy for the amplification / tandem-duplication gate. Supply ploidy directly, or cnv_file – a path to a genome-wide copy-number BED (e.g. the AA-input *_CNV_CALLS.bed) whose width-weighted median CN is used. When ploidy is known and structural QC is on, a bracketed amplicon whose circle-body CN does not exceed min_cn_ratio x ploidy is downgraded (qc_fail = "below_ploidy"): at low copy number a boundary DUP + copy-number step is indistinguishable from an in-place tandem duplication by unphased short-read data, so a genuine ecDNA must be amplified well above ploidy. Both NULL (the default) skips the gate.

min_cn_ratio

Numeric; the circle-body CN must exceed this multiple of ploidy to pass the amplification gate (default 3, matching the PURPLE-native call_simple_excision()).

default_ploidy

Numeric; the ploidy assumed when neither ploidy nor cnv_file resolves a value (default 2, diploid), so the amplification gate still applies an absolute floor of min_cn_ratio x default_ploidy (= 6 at the defaults) rather than being skipped. Set NULL to skip the gate when ploidy is unknown. When the fallback is used, ploidy_assumed is TRUE.

A bridged/ambiguous downgrade applies even when a bracketing boundary DUP exists: if the amplicon's highest read-pair-support junction (a breakend inside the ecDNA extent) has its other breakend on the same chromosome, > bridge_gap beyond the extent, and in an amplified segment, the dominant rearrangement co-mobilises a co-amplified region, so status is set to "bridged" and episomal to FALSE. Cross-chromosome TRAs are the chimeric-episome signature and are NOT downgraded.

Value

A one-row data.table::data.table with episomal (logical; TRUE only for a clean episome), status ("episomal"/"bridged"/"complex"), chimeric (logical), n_chr (chromosomes spanned by the ecDNA), the boundary-DUP record bd_chr, bd_lo, bd_hi, bd_pe_support, bd_jcn, bd_homlen (NA when no boundary DUP), bd_occupancy (ecDNA-interval coverage of the boundary-DUP span; the occupancy-guard metric), the structural-QC record bd_circle_cn (width-weighted median CN of the boundary-DUP span), bd_jcn_frac (boundary-DUP jcn ÷ circle CN), bd_src_frac (boundary source-edge CN ÷ circle CN), ploidy (the ploidy used for the gate, resolved or the default_ploidy fallback), ploidy_assumed (logical; TRUE when the fallback was used), cn_over_ploidy (circle CN ÷ ploidy), qc_pass (logical) and qc_fail (;-separated failed checks incl. below_ploidy, NA if passed or QC off), the bridging-junction record bridge_pe_support, bridge_partner (chr:pos of the out-of-amplicon breakend; NA unless downgraded), and n_junctions.

See also

read_ampliconsuite(), call_simple_excision()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(
  graph_file = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_graph.txt",
  intervals  = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_ecDNA_1_intervals.bed")
} # }
